title: Two q-analogues of permutations
key_idea: Two natural statistics on $S_n$ — $\text{inv}(w)$ (inversions, §1.3) and $\text{maj}(w)$ (major index, §1.7) — are **equidistributed**: $\sum_w q^{\text{inv}(w)} = \sum_w q^{\text{maj}(w)} = [n]_q!$. This is MacMahon's theorem. Section 1.10 gives two complementary 'proofs via bijection as words' vs. 'as bijections,' constructing explicit bijections $\phi: S_n \to S_n$ with $\text{inv}(\phi(w)) = \text{maj}(w)$.
summary: **To be filled in when you reach this section.** Two subsections: (1.10.1) the $q$-analogue as bijections ($\text{inv}$ viewpoint, $q$-factorial via inversion tables, Foata's map); (1.10.2) the $q$-analogue as words ($\text{maj}$ viewpoint, MacMahon's theorem, the bijection $\phi$ of Foata and Schützenberger). These connect directly to Example 2.2.5 in §2.2 ($q$-multinomials).
